newsitem.title: FRANCE: Unions call 24-hour strike at Shell Berre on Dec 9.
newsitem.headline: Unions call 24-hour strike at Shell Berre on Dec 9.

text.p: Unions have called a 24-hour strike at Royal Dutch/Shell Group's 128,000 barrel-per-day Berre refinery in southern France for next Monday, December 9, a local refinery official said on Wednesday.
The call distributed to refinery staff on Wednesday morning follows an appeal by France's leading trade union, the CFDT, for unspecified action at Shell over company plans to cut costs.
Shell France was not available for official comment.
"There has been a call for a strike on Monday," the official said.
It was not immediately clear whether Shell's other main French plant, the 140,000 bpd refinery at Petit Couronne, was also targeted for a strike.
Workers there held a brief go-slow nearly two weeks ago.
The CFDT called on Tuesday for protests at Shell and Esso over cutbacks similar to the ones which have sparked a total French refinery strike at Elf Aquitaine, now in its seventh day.

It proposed disruption between December 6 and 10 at the 80,000 barrels-per-day Reichstett refinery near Strasbourg, eastern France. The plant is 65-percent owned by Shell and BP France, Elf, Total and Mobil also have stakes.
It said Shell's Berre and Petit Couronne refineries would be hit by some form of action on December 10.

It also said talks were speeding up between France's five main unions on plans to disrupt Esso France plants next week. The Exxon Corp subsidiary announced plans to axe 10 percent of its French refinery staff a few days ago.
Elf refinery workers meanwhile kept up their protest on Wednesday, voting at the Feyzin plant near Lyon to extend the strike for another day. Three Elf plants are affected in all.
